We can use matrices to solve systems of linear equations. To do this, we need to set up the **augmented matrix** for the system.

As an example, let's consider the system of equations below.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\color{red}2}x+{\color{red}5}y={\color{blue}-1} \\ {\color{red}-3}x+{\color{red}7}y={\color{blue}1}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the **coefficient matrix**, which consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{matrix}{\color{red}2} & {\color{red}5} \\ {\color{red}-3} & {\color{red}7}\end{matrix}
$$

Then, we create the **augmented matrix**. This is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\begin{array}{cc|c}{\color{red}2} & {\color{red}5} & {\color{blue}-1} \\ {\color{red}-3} & {\color{red}7} & {\color{blue}1}\end{array}
$$

In the future, we will learn how to use coefficient and augmented matrices to solve systems of equations. But for now, let's practice setting them up.

What is the coefficient matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=1 \\ 2y &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

First, we organize the system so that every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=1 \\ 0x+2y &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\left\lbrack
	\begin{matrix}
		1 & -2  \\
		0 & 2 
	\end{matrix}
	\right\rbrack
$$

Using the variables $x$, $y$, and $z,$ then, the corresponding system of equations is

$$\left\{\begin{aligned}0x+y-z &=1 \\ x-y+0z &=1 \\ -x+0y+z &=1.\end{aligned}\right.$$

By simplifying, we obtain

$$\left\{\begin{aligned}y-z &=1 \\ x-y &=1 \\ -x+z &=1.\end{aligned}\right.$$

What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}\frac{c}{2} &=a \\ 5+3b-a &=4c \\ d &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $a,b,c,d$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-a+0b+\frac{1}{2}c+0d &=0 \\ -a+3b-4c+0d &=-5 \\ 0a+0b+0c+d &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}-1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

What is the coefficient matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{1} &=3{x}_{3} \\ -11{x}_{3} &=12\end{aligned}\right.
$$

First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient: 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} &=0 \\ 0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}-11{x}_{3} &=12\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}4 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -11\end{bmatrix}
$$

What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations? 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}a-c &=4b \\ 3c-11a &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $a,b,c$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}a-4b-c &=0 \\ -11a+0b+3c &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -4 & -1 \\ -11 & 0 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -4 & -1 & 0 \\ -11 & 0 & 3 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{2}a &=6b \\ 2a-7b &=5 \\ 2a-4b+\frac{3}{2} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $a,b$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{2}a-6b &=0 \\ 2a-7b &=5 \\ 2a-4b &=-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{c|c}\frac{7}{2} & -6 \\ 2 & -7 \\ 2 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}\frac{7}{2} & -6 & 0 \\ 2 & -7 & 5 \\ 2 & -4 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{array}\right]
$$

What is the augmented matrix for the following system of linear equations?

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}m+5n &=11 \\ 0 &=4n-8 \\ n &=-6m+\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

First, we organize the system so that the variables are ordered $m,n$ on the left-hand side, the constants are on the right-hand side, and every variable has a coefficient:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}m+5n &=11 \\ 0m-4n &=-8 \\ 6m+n &=\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The coefficient matrix consists of the coefficients of the variables:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{c|c}\frac{1}{3} & 5 \\ 0 & -4 \\ 6 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

The augmented matrix is the coefficient matrix augmented with the column that represents the right-hand sides of the equations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}\frac{1}{3} & 5 & 11 \\ 0 & -4 & -8 \\ 6 & 1 & \frac{2}{5}\end{array}\right]
$$
